_comment: Coast shape of the continent footprint (docs/coasts.md). Every number is here; loaded once at startup. Metres unless stated.
_mode_note: noisy = broken coast; oval = the pure ellipse union of prompt 04 (for comparison and regression)
_fade_note: noise fades to zero at |distance from the coast| = lobe amplitude + bay amplitude + fade_extra

size_classes._small_note: fifth class, only for ellipses with a mean semi-axis under upper_limit_of_r (no mapped ellipse is that small; generated islands are): gentle noise only, lobes and bays scaled by lobe_scale, fine detail limited to detail_of_minor times the minor semi-axis

_blend_note: 0 = gentle, 1 = strong; blend = clamp(0.5 + 0.5 * contrast * noise, 0, 1)
_gain_note: raw noise values are multiplied by this and clamped to [-1, 1] so that the amplitude is the real peak push
_cut_note: an inward cut (bay) is never deeper than this fraction of the distance from its coast point to the medial axis of its ellipse, so a cut cannot cross the middle of a thin ellipse
_internal_note: an ellipse's push is damped to zero where its coast point lies inside another ellipse (an internal coast of the union) and is full once the point is this many metres outside every other ellipse
_gap_note: outward growth of an ellipse at a point is limited to max(0, g/2 - min_sand/2), g = distance to the nearest other continent's nominal coast
_origin_note: noise on the brown islet 99 (the origin lies inside it) is scaled down so the origin keeps at least 20 m of rock around it on every seed
